entries.claim: The documented handling of an absent `outstanding` field is not implemented by the routing rules, so an older status seam is effectively treated as an empty outstanding set despite the text saying it must not be.
entries.failure_scenario: Run `/cad-progress` against a status producer that predates `outstanding`, with a phase that has a SUMMARY and a newly created undispatched gap plan. The new outstanding row cannot match because the key is absent, and the following plain executed row routes to `/cad-verify {N}`. Thus the gap plan is skipped—the exact failure the new field is meant to prevent—rather than producing a safe compatibility error or conservatively routing to execution.

counter_evidence.note: The prose/routing gap is real, but the failure scenario is unreachable, so the severity is not high. cadence-core/workflows/progress.md and cadence-core/bin/planning/status.mjs ship inside ONE plugin artifact resolved through the same ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, so a status producer predating `outstanding` cannot be paired with a progress.md that names it. The identical always-present wording already ships for `deferred` at progress.md:39-46 with no routing row of its own either, so this text meets the tree standard rather than departing from it.

entries.claim: Selecting the next free plan filename via `ls` before the planner writes it is a check-then-act race and does not ensure the promised no-overwrite behavior.
entries.failure_scenario: Two `/cad-plan --gaps` invocations for the same phase start concurrently when only `PLAN.md` exists. Both list the directory, both select `PLAN-2.md`, and both pass that target to their planners. Whichever planner finishes last overwrites the other gap plan, losing findings or planned work. No reservation, exclusive create, or post-write collision check is specified.

counter_evidence.note: The check-then-act observation is accurate but the promise it is measured against is not the one the file makes. Step 3 promises a new numbered plan rather than an overwrite of the plan ALREADY THERE, and the Why a new file paragraph at lines 30-40 scopes it to the prior run whose reports/plan-1.md reads PLAN COMPLETE - a sequential-history claim, not a concurrency guarantee. No plan-file write path in the tree takes a lock; the two locks that exist (issue-filing.mjs:436 for FILED.md, milestone prune for ARCHIVE.md) guard append-shaped shared files, so requiring one here would be a new repo-wide standard rather than a defect in this diff.
